findings.title: user_signed_up is sent with the reader's email as the distinct id
findings.explanation: The signup action passes the email to track() as the distinct id, while identify and every other server event use users.id. Each sign-up lands on a separate PostHog person keyed by personal data, so the sign-up never joins the reader's onboarding and later events, and the activation funnel from sign-up breaks.

evidence.quote: await track(email, "user_signed_up", { method: "email", plan_intent: planIntent, has_name: !!name });
posthog.identify(user.id, { email: user.email, plan: user.plan, signed_up_at: user.createdAt });

findings.fix: Pass user.id (in scope from db.user.create) as the first argument of track() in signup. Past sign-ups stay on email-keyed persons; note the date in the changelog (SEMANTICS) so the funnel can start from it.

findings.title: invite_sent sends the friend's email and the sender's email as properties
findings.explanation: invitee_email is the friend's email address, and meta is the sender's own email, read from a hidden form field the browser controls. Emails must never be event properties (context.md Privacy), and the sender is already known from the distinct id.

evidence.quote: await track(user.id, "invite_sent", { invitee_email: email, has_note: note.length > 0, meta });

findings.fix: Stop sending invitee_email and meta; drop the hidden meta field. Send an invite_id from the created row instead (see F17).

findings.title: review_submitted and subscription_canceled send text the reader typed
findings.explanation: review_submitted sends the whole review body as review, and subscription_canceled sends the free text of "Anything else?" as detail. Raw typed text is personal data and context.md forbids it; both texts are already stored in the database.

evidence.quote: await track(user.id, "review_submitted", { book_id: bookId, rating, review: body, has_text: body.length > 0 });

findings.fix: Remove review and detail from the calls. Send char_count (body.length) on review_submitted and a detail_char_count on subscription_canceled if the length matters (suggestions S-review and S-detail).

findings.title: search_performed sends the typed query, ignores cookie consent and goes out as "anonymous"
findings.explanation: SearchTracker sends query (the title the reader typed) through forward(), which posts to /api/events whether or not analytics has started, so readers who declined cookies are tracked too. The distinct id is the PostHog id only when posthog has loaded, else the literal "anonymous". The search form is a GET form, so every search is a full page load, and on a full load SearchTracker's effect runs before AnalyticsProvider starts posthog-js: nearly every search, consent or not, goes out under the one id "anonymous", although the page requires sign-in. Through the server relay it also loses the client super property platform, and it uses results_count where the standard name is result_count.
findings.fix: Send char_count instead of query and result_count instead of results_count. Wait until consent is granted and posthog's loaded callback has run, then send through capture() (the browser id is then the identified user.id); or send it from the search page's server side with user.id. New names are additive; drop query.

findings.title: $pageview sends the search text in its URL
findings.explanation: The page-view effect sends $current_url as window.location.href. The search form is a GET form, so every search page view carries /search?q=<the title the reader typed>.
findings.fix: Add a before_send hook in posthog.init that strips q from $current_url, $referrer, $initial_referrer and $initial_current_url, in properties and in $set_once, on every event (posthog-js adds these itself, and the next page's referrer carries the search too).

findings.title: checkout_completed fires on the Pay click, before any payment
findings.explanation: The browser sends checkout_completed as soon as a 16-digit card number is submitted, before the payment request is made, so every attempt, including ones that then fail, counts as completed. It has no status and no payment_id to join it to payment_succeeded, although the id is created inside the payment request's body just below.
findings.fix: Treat the click as an intent: add checkout_submitted (client, with a payment_id created before both the event and the request) and deprecate checkout_completed with replaced_by checkout_submitted; take the outcome from the server (payment_completed, F10). Breaking: add the new event, keep the old one firing with deprecated, replaced_by and a dual_fire_until window (at least 30 days), and a SEMANTICS changelog line.

findings.title: payment_succeeded is sent before the duplicate check and before the payment is written
findings.explanation: The webhook tracks payment_succeeded before it looks for an existing payment with the same id and before the transaction that writes the payment, subscription and plan. A webhook delivered twice counts the revenue twice, and a transaction that fails still counts it.

evidence.quote: await track(userId, "payment_succeeded", { payment_id: id, amount_cents: amountCents, currency, plan: "pro" });
const duplicate = await db.payment.findUnique({ where: { externalId: id } });

findings.fix: Move the track call after the duplicate check returns and after db.$transaction resolves. Changelog SEMANTICS line for the moved moment.

findings.title: payment_succeeded takes its amount from an unverified request the browser sends
findings.explanation: The checkout form posts the payment.succeeded body to the webhook itself, and the route checks no signature and doesn't compare amountCents with PRO_PRICE_CENTS. Anyone can post any amount, so revenue in PostHog can be faked from the browser. It also never checks that userId is the signed-in reader, so anyone can upgrade any account and have it counted.

evidence.quote: const { id, userId, amountCents, currency = "usd" } = event.data ?? {};

findings.fix: Verify the provider's signature in the webhook (or, while it is simulated, set amount_cents from the server's price), and never accept the event from the browser.

findings.title: checkout_failed is a separate failure event, sent from the browser with typed card digits
findings.explanation: Failures go on their own event instead of status on the outcome, so every conversion rate needs a union. invalid_card is a browser refusal before any request and sends card_last4, the last four characters typed into the card field (card data, possibly any text, possibly empty). A network error makes fetch throw, so no checkout_failed is sent and the button stays on Processing.
findings.fix: Stop sending card_last4. Record payment failures as status=failed with failure_reason on the server outcome (payment_completed, F10). The client refusal (invalid_card) has no outcome event: put it on an error event (error_occurred with feature=checkout, error_reason=invalid_card, a new event for the team to approve). Catch the fetch rejection. Deprecate checkout_failed with replaced_by payment_completed for its payment_failed half. Breaking: dual-fire for at least 30 days, with a SEMANTICS changelog line.

findings.title: Failed payments send nothing: no payment outcome with status
findings.explanation: The webhook returns early for every type but payment.succeeded, and payment_succeeded carries no status or failure_reason. Today the only failures are the route's own 400 and 404 answers and a failed write, which only the browser records (checkout_failed reason=payment_failed); once a real provider sends payment.failed, those will be dropped too.

evidence.quote: return NextResponse.json({ received: true, ignored: event.type });

findings.fix: Add payment_completed from the webhook, after the duplicate check and the transaction, with status=success|failed, failure_reason from the route's refusal branches (missing_fields, unknown_user; the provider's codes UNCONFIRMED until there is one), payment_id, amount_cents, currency and plan; deprecate payment_succeeded with replaced_by payment_completed. Breaking: add the new event or property, keep the old one firing with deprecated, replaced_by and a dual_fire_until window (at least 30 days), and a SEMANTICS changelog line.

findings.title: onboarding_completed never fires: the call sits after redirect()
findings.explanation: In addFirstBook, track("onboarding_completed") comes after redirect("/shelves?welcome=1"). redirect() throws, so the line never runs and no reader is ever counted as finishing onboarding.
findings.fix: Move the await track(...) call above the redirect.

findings.title: Onboarding events are sent again when a reader goes back and resubmits a screen
findings.explanation: The onboarding pages only require a session, and the actions save and track whatever the step, so going back to a screen and submitting it again sends a second onboarding_step_completed (and, once F11 is fixed, a second onboarding_completed).

evidence.quote: await db.user.update({ where: { id: user.id }, data: { onboardingStep: 4 } });

findings.fix: Send onboarding_completed only when onboardingStep was below 4 before the update; add is_revisit (user.onboardingStep already past this step) to onboarding_step_completed, or skip the event on a revisit.

findings.title: onboarding_step_completed.step is a number on one screen and text on the other
findings.explanation: The genres screen sends step 1 as a number; the goal screen sends form.get("step"), the string "2" from a hidden input the browser controls. The property splits into two types in PostHog.

evidence.quote: await track(user.id, "onboarding_step_completed", { step: 1, step_name: "genres", genres: picked, genre_count: picked.length });
await track(user.id, "onboarding_step_completed", { step: form.get("step") ?? 2, step_name: "goal", yearly_goal: goal });

findings.fix: Hard-code step: 2 on the goal screen. If text "2" has already been sent, keep step numeric going forward and note the date (type change needs a new name only if the team wants history clean).

findings.title: checkout_started is dropped when /checkout is loaded directly or refreshed
findings.explanation: The checkout form's mount effect runs before AnalyticsProvider's effect starts posthog-js (the provider comes after the page in the layout), so capture() finds posthog not loaded and does nothing. Only readers who reach /checkout by client-side navigation are counted, so the checkout funnel's first step undercounts.
findings.fix: Queue client events until posthog has loaded (capture() can push to a buffer the provider flushes in loaded), or send checkout_started from the server page.

findings.title: checkout_started sends amount as text and has no entry_point
findings.explanation: amount is (amountCents / 100).toFixed(2), the string "5.00" in dollars, while the other billing events send amount_cents as a number. Checkout opens from the settings Upgrade link and the landing page's Pro card, and nothing says which.
findings.fix: Add amount_cents (number) and entry_point (settings | pricing) and deprecate amount; a type change needs the new name.

findings.title: book_added counts shelf updates as adds, and book_shelf_changed misses them
findings.explanation: The book page's addToShelf upserts and always sends book_added, so "Update shelf" on a book already shelved (or a double submit) counts as an add and never as a move. moveShelf sends book_shelf_changed even when the shelf picked is the current one, which the select defaults to.

evidence.quote: await track(user.id, "book_added", { book_id: bookId, shelf, genre: book.genre, source: "book_page" });
await track(user.id, "book_shelf_changed", { book_id: item.bookId, from_shelf: item.shelf, to_shelf: shelf });

findings.fix: In addToShelf, read the existing item first: send book_added only when it was created, book_shelf_changed (with from_shelf) when the shelf really changed, nothing otherwise. In moveShelf, skip the event when from equals to. Changelog SEMANTICS line. Add the book page path to book_shelf_changed's fires_at.

findings.title: invite_sent has no status, no failure reason and no invite id
findings.explanation: Invalid emails and self-invites redirect before any event, so refused invites are invisible, and the created invite's id is thrown away, so the event can't be joined to anything later. The email field is type=email and required, so invalid_email is mostly reachable only by a direct post; self_invite is the real failure.

evidence.quote: await db.invite.create({ data: { userId: user.id, email, note } });

findings.fix: Send invite_sent with status=success|failed and failure_reason=self_invite|invalid_email (only_when status=failed), and invite_id from db.invite.create (only_when status=success).

findings.title: book_added misses the onboarding first book, and the search path leaves out genre
findings.explanation: The first book added in onboarding only calls logEvent, a development console log, so it never reaches PostHog. Quick add from search sends book_added without genre, although book is loaded right there.

evidence.quote: logEvent("book-added", { userId: user.id, bookId: book.id, shelf: "reading", source: "onboarding" });
await track(user.id, "book_added", { book_id: bookId, shelf: "want_to_read", source: "search" });

findings.fix: Send book_added with source=onboarding from addFirstBook, before its redirect, and add onboarding to source's values; add genre: book.genre in quickAdd.

findings.title: book_removed is sent when nothing was removed, and can't be joined to the book
findings.explanation: removeFromShelf sends book_removed after deleteMany whatever it deleted, so a double click or a stale id counts a removal that didn't happen. It carries only item_id from the form: no book_id and no shelf.

evidence.quote: await db.shelfItem.deleteMany({ where: { id: itemId, userId: user.id } });

findings.fix: Read the item first (findFirst with userId), delete it, and send book_removed only when it existed, with book_id and shelf.

findings.title: search_performed fires on every open or reload of /search, not when a search settles
findings.explanation: SearchTracker sends from a mount effect, so opening /search from the nav or the shelves page's Find a book link counts as a search with no title or filter, and a reload or back navigation sends the same search again. query is then empty.
findings.fix: Send only when a title or filter is set, once per distinct search (key on the URL's search string).

findings.title: reset is never called at logout
findings.explanation: Nothing calls posthog.reset(): logout only destroys the session. On a shared browser the next reader keeps the previous reader's distinct id until identify runs, and anything sent before that (and every page view of a logged-out visitor) lands on the previous reader.
findings.fix: Call posthog.reset() on logout (e.g. in the provider when user goes from set to null) and after account deletion.

findings.title: identify writes the reader's email to the PostHog profile
findings.explanation: AnalyticsProvider calls identify with email as a person property on every page load. context.md says never to send emails.

evidence.quote: posthog.identify(user.id, { email: user.email, plan: user.plan, signed_up_at: user.createdAt });

findings.fix: Remove email from identify's properties, unset email on existing profiles, and remove it from _user_properties.yaml. (signed_up_at as set_once is a tidy-up: createdAt never changes.)

findings.title: goal_reminder_sent is probably lost, and is resent on every run
findings.explanation: The weekly job makes its own posthog-node client and never calls flush or shutdown: main() ends with db.$disconnect() and the error path calls process.exit(1), so queued events can be dropped when the process exits. It is sent every run although the row is upserted per reader and week, so a second run in a week counts the same reader again. It bypasses track(), so it has no app_version.
findings.fix: Send through the server wrapper track(), or await posthog.shutdown() on both the success and the error path before exit. Send only for a new week's row: read it with findUnique on userId_weekOf first, or create and catch the unique-constraint error (upsert doesn't say whether it created).

findings.title: goal_reminder_sent says a reminder was sent, but nothing is delivered
findings.explanation: The job only writes a GoalReminder row; nothing in the repo reads it or notifies the reader, while the landing page sells weekly goal reminders.

evidence.quote: features: ["Everything in Free", "Ratings and reviews", "Weekly goal reminders", "Mobile app access"],

findings.fix: Keep the name for now (renaming needs dual-fire); describe it as 'reader flagged behind pace'. When delivery is built, send a reminder_delivered outcome with status.

findings.title: user_signed_up and user_logged_in record only successes
findings.explanation: Refused sign-ups (invalid email, short password, email taken) and refused logins (wrong email or password) redirect before any event, so failure rates are invisible. The browser's required, type=email and minLength checks stop most invalid emails and short passwords, so email_taken and wrong_credentials are the failures that really reach the server.
findings.fix: Add status=success|failed and failure_reason (invalid_email | password_too_short | email_taken; wrong_credentials) with only_when status=failed. The failed path has no user id: send it with the visitor's anonymous id passed from the form, which is a team decision (open question Q2).

findings.title: user_signed_up.plan_intent is always null
findings.explanation: signup reads plan_intent from a form field named plan, but the signup form has no such field; the page reads ?plan= from the URL only to show a note. Sign-ups from the Pro call to action can't be told apart.
findings.fix: Add a hidden input name="plan" with the URL's plan to the signup form, and keep plan in the URL of the error redirects so a retry keeps it.

findings.title: mobile_shelves_fetched records every request as iOS
findings.explanation: platform is hard-coded "ios", so any Android client counts as iOS and the property says nothing. The route also accepts the browser's session cookie, so a browser that opens /api/shelves would be counted as mobile, though no code in the repo calls it from the web.
findings.fix: Set platform from a header the app sends, else the User-Agent; if the request can't tell, drop the property.

findings.title: cta_clicked splits plan by casing and misses the nav Sign up button
findings.explanation: The hero sends plan "pro" and the pricing cards send the display name "Free" or "Pro", so Pro shows as two values. The nav's Sign up link, shown to signed-out visitors on every page, is a call to action into sign-up and sends nothing.

evidence.quote: <TrackLink href={cta} className="btn" event="cta_clicked" properties={{ cta: "hero", plan: "pro", is_logged_in: !!user }}>

findings.fix: Send plan: plan.name.toLowerCase() on the cards, and use TrackLink with cta="nav" for the nav Sign up link (plan only_when cta is hero or plan_card; add nav to cta's values and a fires_at entry). Enum casing change: add the lower-case values and note the date.

findings.title: $pageview counts the first page of each visit twice
findings.explanation: posthog.init has capture_pageview: true and the provider's effect also captures $pageview once ready, so the first page after analytics starts is sent twice.
findings.fix: Set capture_pageview: false (the effect already sends every route change), or drop the effect and use capture_pageview: 'history_change'.

findings.title: account_deleted is sent before the account is deleted
findings.explanation: deleteAccount tracks before destroySession and db.user.delete, so a delete that fails is still counted.
findings.fix: Move the track call after db.user.delete; plan and createdAt are already in memory from requireUser().

findings.title: reading_goal_updated is sent when the goal didn't change
findings.explanation: The settings input starts with the current goal and updateGoal never compares, so pressing Save without editing counts as a change.

evidence.quote: await track(user.id, "reading_goal_updated", { old_goal: user.yearlyGoal, new_goal: goal });

findings.fix: Skip the update and the event when goal equals user.yearlyGoal.

findings.title: Opening the cancel flow isn't tracked
findings.explanation: subscription_canceled records the outcome, but no event records a Pro reader opening /settings/cancel. A $pageview funnel can approximate it, but page views depend on consent and are doubled on the first page (F29).
findings.fix: Add subscription_cancel_started, sent when the cancel page opens for a Pro reader, paired with subscription_canceled.

findings.title: invite_sent says an invite was sent, but nothing reaches the friend
findings.explanation: sendInvite only stores the invite: no email or link goes out and there is no way to accept it, and the page says "Invite saved." The event can't be read as the friend being contacted or used for invite-to-signup conversion.

evidence.quote: await db.invite.create({ data: { userId: user.id, email, note } });

findings.fix: Keep the name (a rename needs dual-fire); say in the description that nothing is delivered. When delivery and acceptance are built, add invite_delivered and invite_accepted outcomes.

questions.question: checkout_completed is sent on the Pay click. How should checkout be tracked going forward?

options.text: Add checkout_submitted for the click and payment_completed from the webhook as the outcome; deprecate checkout_completed and checkout_failed with a 30-day dual-fire
Keep checkout_completed's name but move it to the webhook after the payment is written

questions.why: The name says completed but nothing has completed; a new intent and a server outcome keep the old charts readable while they move over.

questions.question: Refused sign-ups and logins have no user id. Which id should a failed user_signed_up or user_logged_in be sent with?

options.text: Pass the browser's PostHog anonymous id in a hidden form field and send the failure from the server action with it; when the visitor declined cookies there is no id, and the failure is not sent
Send failures from the browser on the error redirect instead
Don't track failed sign-ups and logins

questions.why: The server knows the failure reason; the anonymous id joins it to the visitor's later successful sign-up.

questions.question: Event naming: every Shelfie event is snake_case object_action (user_signed_up, book_added); the only exception is PostHog's own $pageview. Which convention should events follow?

options.text: snake_case object_action, two words or more, allowing PostHog's own $-prefixed events (naming.event_pattern: '^\$?[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)+$')
snake_case object_action, two words or more, as now (naming.event_pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)+$'), with $pageview left as a known exception

questions.why: All 20 of the team's multi-word events already use snake_case; $pageview is the vendor's name and can't change.

calls.quote: await track(email, "user_signed_up", { method: "email", plan_intent: planIntent, has_name: !!name });

fires.why: The signup server action is posted by the form on /signup (app/signup/page.tsx:22); the call is on the success path after the three validation redirects, so it is reachable. No data to say whether it arrives.

moment.why: On the server after db.user.create resolves and createSession sets the cookie, before redirect; the three refusal branches redirect (which throws) before it.

paths.why: signup in app/actions/auth.ts is the only place that creates a user (db.user.create appears nowhere else); /signup is the only form that posts to it.

once.why: One awaited call per request in a server action; a resubmit of the same email hits the existing-user redirect at :22 and sends nothing.

name_accurate.why: The user row exists and the session is created when it fires.

name_clear.why: snake_case object_action; no other sign-up event in the plan.

properties.why: A sign-up can fail on the server (email taken, invalid email, short password) but the event has no status or failure_reason: every refusal redirects before the call, so the sign-up funnel can't show how many attempts fail or why.

values_filled.why: plan_intent is read from a form field named plan, but the /signup form has no plan field: the page reads ?plan= from the URL and only uses it for a note, never putting it in the form. So plan_intent is null on every sign-up, including those that came from a plan call to action (/signup?plan=pro and /signup?plan=free from the home page).

values_sensible.why: The event is sent with the reader's email as the PostHog distinct id, while identify (client) and every other server event use users.id. The sign-up lands on a separate person keyed by an email (personal data as an id, against the team's privacy rule), so it never joins the reader's later events and sign-up to activation funnels break. user.id is in scope two lines above.

evidence.quote: await track(email, "user_signed_up", { method: "email", plan_intent: planIntent, has_name: !!name });
posthog.identify(user.id, { email: user.email, plan: user.plan, signed_up_at: user.createdAt });

could_carry.why: Only email, password and name are in scope besides what is sent; none can be sent. Nothing at the call site answers a new question.

calls.quote: await track(user.id, "user_logged_in", { onboarding_step: user.onboardingStep, resumed_onboarding: user.onboardingStep < 4 });

fires.why: The login server action is posted by the form on /login (app/login/page.tsx:19); the call follows the password check on the success path, so it is reachable. No data to say whether it arrives.

moment.why: On the server after verifyPassword succeeds and createSession resolves; the wrong-credentials branch redirects (throws) at :38 before it.

paths.why: login is the only place that creates a session for an existing user (createSession is called only here and in signup); the mobile API reads bearer tokens but issues none.

once.why: One awaited call per request in a server action.

name_accurate.why: The session exists when it fires.

name_clear.why: snake_case object_action; no near-duplicate in the plan.

properties.why: A login can fail (unknown email or wrong password) but the event has no status or failure_reason; the refusal redirects before the call, so failed logins can't be counted.

values_filled.why: user is non-null after the check at :37; onboardingStep is a non-null Int with default 1 (prisma/schema.prisma:19).

values_sensible.why: onboarding_step is the numeric onboardingStep, 1 to 4 as the onboarding actions set it, matching values: [1, 2, 3, 4]; resumed_onboarding is a boolean derived from it; distinct id is user.id, the id identify uses.

could_carry.why: user.plan is in scope and the plan user property is only set from the client after cookie consent.

fires.why: deleteAccount is posted by the delete form on /settings; the call follows the DELETE confirmation check, so it is reachable.

moment.why: Sent before destroySession and db.user.delete: a delete that throws afterwards is still counted as a deleted account. The outcome should be sent after db.user.delete resolves (user.id, plan and createdAt are still in scope).

paths.why: deleteAccount is the only place a user row is deleted.

once.why: One awaited call per request; after it the session is gone, so a resubmit is redirected by requireUser.

name_accurate.why: Nothing is deleted yet when it fires (same cause as moment).

name_clear.why: snake_case object_action; no near-duplicate.

properties.why: plan and days_since_signup on the single path.

values_filled.why: user comes from requireUser (non-null); plan is a non-null String with default free; createdAt is non-null.

values_sensible.why: plan is free | pro (schema comment); days_since_signup is a whole number of days computed as a number, not text.

could_carry.why: Tier other; no suggestion.

fires.why: CheckoutForm is rendered by app/checkout/page.tsx:16 for every free reader; the useEffect at :12 runs on mount. capture() is a no-op until cookie consent starts posthog-js.

moment.why: An intent event on mount of the checkout form, after the server page has redirected Pro readers away (page.tsx:8); the right side (client) for an intent.

paths.why: Lost on a full page load or refresh of /checkout: React runs the page's effects (inside <main>) before AnalyticsProvider's init effect, which sits after {children} in app/layout.tsx, so capture() sees posthog.__loaded false and returns. It only arrives when the reader reaches /checkout by client-side navigation (Upgrade to Pro link in settings, plan card on the home page).

once.why: One effect with a numeric dependency (amountCents, a server constant), so it runs once per mount; a re-visit is a new intent by design.

name_accurate.why: The checkout form is on screen when it fires.

name_clear.why: object_action, snake_case; checkout_completed is its pair, not a duplicate.

properties.why: Checkout has two ways in (the Upgrade to Pro link in settings and the Pro plan card on the home page) but no entry_point, so nobody can tell which surface drives upgrades.

values_filled.why: plan is the literal "pro"; amountCents is PRO_PRICE_CENTS (500) passed from the server page, never undefined.

values_sensible.why: amount is sent as text in dollars ("5.00") from toFixed(2), while checkout_completed and payment_succeeded send amount_cents as a number: sums break and the same price lives under two names and units.

could_carry.why: Only userId and amountCents are in scope at the call; nothing else answers a new question (entry_point is raised under properties).

fires.why: Reached in onSubmit for any 16-digit card once posthog-js has started (after consent).

moment.why: Sent from the browser on submit, before the payment request at :31 is even sent: every attempt counts as completed, including the ones that then fail at :47. A money outcome belongs on the server after the payment is recorded; it is also dropped for readers who declined cookies.

paths.why: The checkout form is the only way to pay; the one submit handler sends it.

once.why: One call per submit, and the button is disabled while the request is pending.

name_accurate.why: Nothing is completed when it fires: the payment hasn't been requested yet. It is a checkout_submitted intent.

name_clear.why: object_action, snake_case; no other event uses the name.

properties.why: Presented as the checkout outcome but has no status or failure_reason, and no payment_id to join it to payment_succeeded, although the id is generated three lines later.

values_filled.why: book is non-null past the redirect at line 46; book.id and book.genre (String, not optional in the schema) are always set.

values_sensible.why: book_id is the book row id, genre the book's genre from the catalogue (the GENRES list), no personal data.

could_carry.why: No other value at the call site answers a question this event can't; the goal and genres are already on the step events.

How long after signing up do readers upgrade to Pro?

property_suggestions.question: How many cancelling readers explain themselves, and does it differ by reason?
Do readers who write longer reviews come back more, and how long are reviews (in place of sending the text)?
How many landing-page CTA clicks lead to sign-up versus straight to checkout (an upgrade) or the shelves?
How many of these fetches really come from the mobile app (bearer token) rather than a browser session cookie?
Do mobile readers open the app while they are actively reading a book (books on the Reading shelf), or only to browse what they want to read?
On the goal screen, do readers keep the suggested goal of 12 or set their own? (goal !== user.yearlyGoal, step_name=goal only)
How many step completions are readers going back to change an answer rather than moving forward? (user.onboardingStep already past this step)

baselined.why: Sent by a command-line job (npm run job:goal-check), which follows no HTTP request; fires_at says how to run it in from

not_proposed.action: Reader logs out
not_proposed.reason: No product question an event answers. But logout needs an identity reset (posthog.reset in the client): _identity.yaml has no reset key and nothing calls reset, so the next reader on the same browser keeps the previous reader's distinct id until identify runs.

not_proposed.action: Cancel form rejected (no reason picked, or Other without detail)
not_proposed.reason: Validation redirects on a required field (the radio is HTML-required, so the first can't happen from the form); a refusal before the work, which subscription_cancel_started without subscription_canceled already shows as drop-off.

not_proposed.action: Cancel submitted with no active subscription
not_proposed.reason: Only a stale tab or a second submit reaches it; nothing changes and nobody decides anything from it.

not_proposed.action: Upgrade to Pro link in settings
not_proposed.reason: Navigation into checkout; checkout_started covers the intent and should carry entry_point=settings instead of its own event.

not_proposed.action: Cancel subscription link in settings
not_proposed.reason: Navigation into the cancel flow; covered by the proposed subscription_cancel_started.

not_proposed.action: Welcome to Pro / subscription canceled confirmation banners
not_proposed.reason: Screen state after an outcome the server already sends; no decision rides on the view.

not_proposed.action: Weekly goal-check job run completes (users checked, number behind)
not_proposed.reason: Job health is ops monitoring, not a product question; per-reader outcomes are already goal_reminder_sent.

evidence.quote: console.log(`Checked ${users.length} users; ${behind} behind pace for week of ${weekOf.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.`);

not_proposed.action: Goal progress shown on /shelves ('N of goal books finished this year')
not_proposed.reason: Screen view with no decision; autocapture page views cover it.

not_proposed.action: Delivering the goal reminder to the reader (email/notification)
not_proposed.reason: No delivery exists in the code; when one is built it should send the outcome (goal_reminder_sent with status/failure_reason, or rename via deprecation) — raised under goal_reminder_sent.name_accurate.

not_proposed.action: Invite refused (email without @, self-invite)
not_proposed.reason: Not a separate event: it belongs on invite_sent as status=failed with failure_reason=invalid_email|self_invite (raised as the invite_sent.properties problem).

not_proposed.action: Opens the invite page / views the list of sent invites
not_proposed.reason: A screen view with no decision; autocapture covers it, and invite_sent with status measures the flow.

not_proposed.action: Clicks the Invite link in the nav
not_proposed.reason: Navigation with one entry point; the invite form cannot be abandoned mid-flow in a way an intent event would reveal beyond page views.

not_proposed.action: Opens a book's page
not_proposed.reason: A screen view with no decision on it; $pageview already covers it, and the actions taken there (add to shelf, review) have their own events.

not_proposed.action: Review refused (no rating, or book not on the Finished shelf)
not_proposed.reason: The rating radio is required in the form and the review page redirects away unless the book is finished, so these branches are only reached by a hand-crafted request; no question needs them.

not_proposed.action: Quick add or add to shelf fails (book not found, unknown shelf)
not_proposed.reason: Thrown errors only reachable with a tampered form (ids and shelves come from the page); an error tracker matter, not analytics.

evidence.quote: if (!book) throw new Error("Book not found");

not_proposed.action: Visitor clicks 'Log in' in the nav
not_proposed.reason: Marketing-site navigation, not a call into sign-up; the login outcome is user_logged_in on the server.

not_proposed.action: Visitor accepts or declines cookies
not_proposed.reason: Dismissing a banner; a decline can't be sent (no consent) and an accept only shows as the analytics starting, so the event would answer nothing reliably.

not_proposed.action: Unauthorized request refused (401)
not_proposed.reason: An auth refusal on a read endpoint with no known user to attach it to; expired tokens and probes carry no product decision, and it belongs in server logs, not analytics.

not_proposed.action: Completes the third onboarding screen (first book) with no onboarding_step_completed step 3
not_proposed.reason: onboarding_completed is this screen's completion event (once moved before the redirect); a step-3 event would double-count the same moment.

not_proposed.action: Onboarding screen refuses the answer (no genre picked, goal outside 1 to 365, no book picked)
not_proposed.reason: Validation refusals before any work; the browser's required/min/max already block most, and drop-off shows as a missing next step event. Raise later if the drop-off needs explaining.

not_proposed.action: Signed-in reader lands on an onboarding screen (signup redirect or login resume)
not_proposed.reason: The start is user_signed_up and user_logged_in (resumed_onboarding); screen views carry no decision and $pageview covers them.
